primary_task: Turn an observation into a documented set of candidate hypotheses, rival explanations, discriminating predictions, measurements and a preregistration-ready analysis plan, with a dated evidence boundary.

requirements.name: python3 (3.11+, standard library; bundled scripts)
requirements.evidence:
Do not treat a convenient proxy as the construct itself. Validate with:

```bash
python3 scripts/check_operationalization.py local-operationalization.json
```
requirements.basis: run shell commands on Linux x86_64: ... build, test, run CLIs and scripts (python3 is standard software of the Linux platform; Python versions also installable: "apt from Ubuntu")

requirements.name: web search (literature search)
requirements.evidence: Search before making literature-dependent statements. Prefer primary research, official policies, primary methods papers, current reporting guidelines, and systematic reviews used for orientation.
requirements.basis: search the public web and read result snippets

requirements.name: arxiv.org / export.arxiv.org
requirements.evidence: When network access is available, fetch https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.00065 (or http://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2609.00065) before writing the reference
requirements.basis: other hosts are refused (for example huggingface, Microsoft Learn and Azure, Cloudflare, Expo, Neon and NVIDIA)

requirements.name: human authorization / ethics review
requirements.evidence: Before using unpublished, sensitive, controlled, personal, proprietary, export-controlled, or security-relevant material: 1. Confirm authorization
requirements.basis: ask the user a question (with options) and read the answer in the conversation

notes: The bundled CLIs are stdlib-only and local; the document states they 'require no network, credentials, models'. Literature search uses web_search (snippets only); full-text access to many publishers is outside the allow-list, which may limit the evidence boundary but the document says to record access limitations. The arXiv fetch is conditional ('When network access is available') and only for citing the skill in a manuscript, so it is not hard. Other reading: if full-text fetching of primary sources is required for the evidence boundary, those publisher hosts are outside the allow-list (unavailable) and the verdict could be BLOCKED; I took web_search snippets plus recorded limitations as sufficient.
